title: If from '97 onwards, Matt Damon and Leonardo Dicaprio switched all their biggest films with one another, who'd come off best?

commenti.body: Both are for the most part solid actors but I wouldn’t say they are capable of ‘disappearing’ into a role.  I slightly prefer Damon because he has a James Stewart like-ability about him and DiCaprio (especially in period films) feels like a kid playing dress up in a school play.  But to be fair neither of them have ever made a film worse by being in it and they have a really good track record of choosing good scripts with good directors.

I think both careers take a little bit. They are different types of actors and pretty good at picking their roles.

DiCaprior excels as a pretty boy who is out of control with very high maintenance emotions, and he takes on these larger-than-life command-the-screen performances as a result.

That’s not Damon’s style, he’s better as a complicated introvert when you can’t truly see what he’s thinking/feeling/going through, a character unable to verbalize his emotions, which is in stark contrast to Leo, who is going to tell everyone what he’s thinking even if he’s just looking at a mirror. Damon is more physical and gritty, he can play dangerous better.

Now I just want to see a reshoot of The Departed where they switch roles. They should've done it like Clue where half of people who see it in theatres see each version.

In all honesty, I think Damon would struggle in a couple Dicaprio roles, but Dicaprio would not struggle in Damon roles. Namely, I don't see Damon pulling off the free-spirited Jack Dawson role, as I don't think I've seen him do any similar ones. I also think Leo is better at phony/charismatic roles such as Gatsby and the *Django* role.

Interesting question but as you mentioned Bill Simmons is just wrong here lol.

There’s roles like Invictus, true grit and the Bourne series that I don’t think Leo could pull off. On the flip side, I don’t think any actor could pull off the wolf of Wall Street and that includes Damon. 

Both are great actors, and have made some incredible movies, just look at those lists.
Agreed, I don’t think Leo would be very believable as Bourne. Similarly I can’t see Damon doing some of the more excessive roles like Wolf of Wall Street very well.

>any actor could pull off the wolf of Wall Street and that includes Damon.

I don't know about "any actor", but I do agree that Damon would've been miscast in that role

Including Saving Private Ryan seems dubious at best, sure he's the titular Ryan but he's also barely in the movie and I wouldn't say his short time in the movie is some tour de force of acting. 

I'd switch Saving Private Ryan with Rounders, while it doesn't have the same pedigree as Saving Private Ryan it is squarely a Matt Damon starring vehicle, one where he is VERY good in but also a role I can see Leo doing in a very different way (more cold, less reluctant to dive back into gambling) and the idea of DiCaprio and Edward Norton playing off each other is an intoxicating idea.

As to answer your question:

I think more roles are written/conceived with "Leo in mind" than they are with Damon, how you feel about both actor's abilities aside so it might be harder to Damon to fit in those roles. It's hard for me to see Damon doing roles like Amsterdam in Gangs of New York or Calvin Candie in Django. That said Damon's strength is he's an extremely malleable actor, able to due everything from straight character dramas, to pulpy period pieces to being an action star. I don't think DiCaprio has been given the opportunity to flex those muscles and to be honest I can't imagine an actor of his caliber to not be able to do something like The Bourne Identity (I'm not really counting his role in Inception as being an action star since most of his co stars did most of the action) 

I'd say they both do well, but DiCaprio's Bourne doesn't do as well (I think Damon brings a LOT to those movies that isn't part of the acting muscle's we've seen DiCaprio flex) so he doesn't take that action detour Damon did with movies like Green Zone and Elysium. I also don't think he'd work in Ocean's 11 as Damon's Linus needed that innocence and naivety that Damon tapped into that post The Beach DiCaprio seems nearly unable to reach other. Either the character gets heavily rewritten for him or he gets recasted for sequels (or he just never takes the part.)

I just cannot see Damon pulling off some of the more “evil” roles DiCaprio can. Django and wolf of Wall Street specifically. I do think he could have pulled off OUATIH and any of the action or horror stuff DiCaprio has done. Then on the inverse I don’t think DiCaprio could have done air Or Oppenheimer, the Martian or ford. Vs Ferrari. 

I think Damon is really good at playing smart people who still can be “normal” and charming. Plus he’s good at playing dopey people. DiCaprio is better at playing evil or asshole types

>Django and wolf of Wall Street

I actually think Damon can play evil very well, but Candie would've had to been re-written for Damon, something that Tarantino would've gladly done, assuming he was hellbent on casting him. His villain would be less of a snarling bad guy, and more of a sinister charmer with a mean-streak

But Wolf of Wall Street is a lost cause, I just can't see Damon pulling Belfort off

>Namely, I don't see Damon pulling off the free-spirited Jack Dawson role, as I don't think I've seen him do any similar ones.

I actually think Damon would've nailed Jack Dawson, he could play charming very well (especially when he was younger). He would've also made Jack more real, and made the differences in the social stature between him and first class, far more palpable

But he wouldn't have become the "dream man" of an entire generation of women, so there's that

I think Damon can do most Leo roles, like he would have been excellent in Blood Diamond and all of the thrillers and Don't Look Up, but there's no way Leo can do Behind the Candelabra or any of the comedies like Dogma. Matt is also more naturally charming so GWH and anything with romance is more in Damon's wheelhouse. Apart from Titanic, I don't find Leo's romances or his attempt at comedy to be convincing. Damon is far more versatile.
[removed]

> He would've also made Jack more real

I agree with this, but I wouldn't have liked that as much. For me, part of Jack Dawson's greatness comes from the fact that he almost seems too perfect for the situation to be real. Like he's the *exact* mentor the protagonist (Rose) needed at the time. In other words, he's literally the man of her dreams. He pops into her life, doesn't change as a character at all throughout the story, and then disappears.

Don’t know if this is true but I read Leo liked the script and told Scorsese he didn’t know which character he should play, and Scorsese chose Billy for him.

That’s what James Cameron wanted, so the Damon version makes zero sense. Jack is the manic pixie dream boy of rose’s dreams and I have a hard time thinking there would ever be a world with Damonmania.
No one would be hell bent on casting Damon if they have Leo. Every single role Damon has done with the exception of the films he wrote for himself I guarantee the director wanted Leo

Considering "The Talented Mr. Ripley", I think people might be underestimating Matt Damon's ability to portray evil/wicked characters. I believe both actors would be able to switch fairly well, but then Matt Damon would be more well-regarded than he is currently (likewise, Leo DiCaprjo wouldn't have the same notoriety).

The Departed, Blood Diamond has Body of Lies has a lot of action
I mean Body of Lies is pretty bad though...

I’ll be more clear on my point, I think Leo’s best role is Jordan Belfort, and I think it’s the best acting performance of the 21st century. NYT critic Richard Brody said this recently and I completely agree.

DiCaprio would struggle mightily with every Damon role. He’s too theatrical and handsome. 

DiCaprio stuck alone on Mars would be insufferable and exhausting, you wouldn’t give a shit about his rescue. You’d be rooting for him to lose at the end of Rounders and Worm would come across as a sympathetic voice of reason. He’s stick out like a sore thumb with the Good Will Hunting crew. He’d have no camaraderie with Ben Affleck in any movie. And as Jason Bourne he’d have some weird facial hair and you’d be like “I’m pretty sure I could kick this guy’s ass.”

Matt Damon plays an exceptional villain. He plays very complicated, real people who have some reasoning behind their actions and their flaws push them into villainy. 

Leo plays a “steal the show” villain, a bad guy who’s so bad they make the movie more exciting exciting.
